questions.stem_markdown: A junior doctor reviewing a 15-year-old with recurrent headaches says he has covered **Home, Education, Activities, Drugs, Sexuality, and mood**. According to the notes, which additional group of issues should still be included in the adolescent assessment?

options.text: Sleep, safety, spirituality, and social media
Vaccination history, travel history, dental history, and bowel habit
Birth history, developmental milestones, bowel habit, and hearing
Screen time, allergies, urine output, and immunisation status
Spirituality, bowel habit, hearing, and growth chart review

questions.explanation_markdown: The HEEADSS block in the notes extends beyond the core traditional headings and explicitly includes **sleep, safety, spirituality, and social media**. That makes option A the best fit.

why_others_wrong.B: These may be relevant in some consultations, but they are not the additional grouped topics listed in the HEEADSS section of the notes.
why_others_wrong.C: This set is not the extension to HEEADSS described in the source material.
why_others_wrong.D: Some of these topics may matter clinically, but this is not the note-based completion of the adolescent psychosocial assessment.
why_others_wrong.E: Spirituality appears in the notes, but this option does not match the specific grouped additions listed there.

key_takeaways: HEEADSS in the notes includes more than the older core acronym alone.
Sleep, safety, spirituality, and social media are explicitly listed additional domains.
A structured psychosocial screen helps avoid missing important adolescent issues.

questions.stem_markdown: A 14-year-old spends much of the consultation talking about **who she is becoming**, wanting more independence, and struggling to manage intense changing feelings. Which developmental domain is **most directly represented** in the notes?

options.text: Physical/biological
Cognitive
Emotional
Social
Moral/ethical

questions.explanation_markdown: The developmental-tasks section describes the **emotional** domain as involving **identity formation, independence, and managing emotions**. That matches this vignette more closely than the other domains.

why_others_wrong.A: Physical and biological development refers to puberty, sexual maturation, and body image development rather than the identity-and-emotion focus of this stem.
why_others_wrong.B: The cognitive domain in the notes centres on abstract thinking, problem-solving, and future planning.
why_others_wrong.D: Social development focuses more on peer relationships, intimacy, separation from parents, and experimentation with roles.
why_others_wrong.E: Moral and ethical development is described as growth in personal values, autonomy, and responsibility rather than the identity-and-emotion focus here.

key_takeaways: Identity formation is placed within emotional development in the notes.
Adolescent development spans distinct but overlapping domains.
Separating emotional from social or moral development improves clinical interpretation.

questions.stem_markdown: A 15-year-old says, "There is no point trying to improve things at school because whether things go badly or well is just luck." Which clinician response best supports the **resilience factor** highlighted in the notes?

options.text: You are probably right, because most outcomes are outside your control anyway
Let’s choose one step that is in your control this week and review how it goes
Try not to think about school until the stress settles on its own
Your parents should take over these decisions because they understand the situation better
The main goal is to accept that effort usually does not change much

questions.explanation_markdown: The resilience section explicitly lists **internal locus of control** as a protective factor. A response that focuses on one achievable action within the adolescent’s control aligns best with that note-based principle.

why_others_wrong.A: This reinforces an external locus of control rather than the resilience factor named in the notes.
why_others_wrong.C: Avoidance does not build the sense of control highlighted in the source material.
why_others_wrong.D: Adult support matters, but this option shifts control away from the young person rather than strengthening it.
why_others_wrong.E: This directly undermines the resilience concept of internal control.

key_takeaways: Internal locus of control is listed in the notes as a resilience factor.
Counselling can strengthen resilience by focusing on controllable next steps.
Small achievable actions can be more useful than global reassurance.

questions.stem_markdown: A 13-year-old says vaping and weekend drinking with friends are harmless because "the brain is already grown by secondary school". Which reply is **most consistent** with the notes?

options.text: Brain development is mostly complete by early adolescence, so the main concern is school discipline
The adolescent brain is still developing and is susceptible to the addictive effects of alcohol and other drugs
Substances only become medically important once daily use has already developed
The main risk from early substance use is legal trouble rather than brain effects
Only adolescents with existing mental illness are biologically vulnerable to substance-related harm

questions.explanation_markdown: The notes state that adolescence is a period of major brain development and specifically say that the **developing brain is susceptible to the addictive effects of alcohol and other drugs**. That makes option B the best answer.

why_others_wrong.A: The source material explicitly describes ongoing brain development during adolescence rather than completion by early secondary school.
why_others_wrong.C: The notes do not say biological concern begins only once daily use is present.
why_others_wrong.D: The source material specifically highlights brain susceptibility, not just social or legal consequences.
why_others_wrong.E: The notes do not limit vulnerability to adolescents who already have mental illness.

key_takeaways: The adolescent brain is still developing.
The notes specifically highlight susceptibility to addictive effects of alcohol and other drugs.
Early counselling about substance use should be framed around development, not just rules.
